mainTopic: Identifying biblical places (רקת, קטרון, עקרון) and the opposing fortunes of קסרי (Rome) and ירושלים
overview: This amud matches place names from תנ״ך with cities known in the time of the גמרא. It starts by identifying חמת, רקת and כנרת. רבא proves from eulogies said in טבריא that רקת is טבריא, and two explanations are given for why the city is also called טבריא. Next, זעירא says קטרון is ציפורי. The גמרא challenges him: קטרון was in זבולון's portion, and זבולון complained about his land, yet ציפורי was very fertile. Along the way it tells how הקדוש ברוך הוא comforted זבולון with the treasures of his sea and sand. The answer is that זבולון still wanted flat fields and vineyards like נפתלי had. The amud then reads verses about עקרון as being about קסרי, the Roman capital, and teaches that קסרי and ירושלים always have opposite fortunes. It ends with רבי יצחק's teachings about עשו, and the last of these continues on the next amud.

steps.title: First identification: חמת is טבריא, רקת is ציפורי
steps.stepSummary: The speaker, continuing his statement on the previous amud, says the elders confirmed his view. He identifies חמת as טבריא, רקת as ציפורי, and כנרת as גינוסר, and explains each name.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it turned out the way I said. חמת is טבריא. Why is it called חמת? Because of the hot springs of טבריא. רקת is ציפורי. Why is it called רקת? Because it sits high up, like a riverbank. כנרת is גינוסר. Why is it called כנרת? Because its fruit is as sweet as the sound of a harp.
steps.whatsHappening: The speaker from the previous line finishes his statement. He says the elders agreed with him, then explains which modern city matches each biblical name and why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each identification gets a name explanation. חמת comes from the hot springs (חמי) of טבריא. רקת comes from 'רקתא', a riverbank, because ציפורי sits high like a raised bank. כנרת comes from 'כינור', a harp, because the fruit of גינוסר is so sweet. The key claim here is that רקת is ציפורי, not טבריא, and the next step attacks exactly that point.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was found to be like my view (the elders agreed with me)
The hot springs of Tiberias
The bank of a river
Harps / lyres
It is raised up / elevated

phrases.english: and it was found in accordance with my opinion.
phrases.notes: This finishes a statement from the previous amud: he asked the elders, and they agreed with him.

phrases.english: Hammath is Tiberias,
and why was it called Hammath?
On account of the hot springs of Tiberias.
Rakkath is Tzippori,
and why was it called Rakkath?
Because it is raised up like the bank of a river.
Chinnereth is Ginosar,
and why was it called Chinnereth?
Because its fruit is sweet like the sound of harps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a statement begun in the preceding text of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חמת = טבריא, רקת = ציפורי, כנרת = גינוסר, each with a name explanation.

steps.title: רבא objects: everyone knows רקת is טבריא
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges the claim that רקת is ציפורי. He brings two eulogy formulas used in טבריא that call the city 'רקת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Is there really anyone who says רקת is not טבריא? When a great man dies here in בבל, they eulogize him there with: 'He was great in ששך (בבל), and he had a name in רקת.' And when they bring a coffin up there, they eulogize: 'Lovers of the survivors, residents of רקת, go out and receive the dead from the deep (low-lying בבל).'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the previous identification. He says it is obvious that רקת is טבריא, and he points to how people in טבריא actually speak at funerals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The target is the claim 'רקת זו ציפורי'. רבא's evidence is living usage: the eulogizers in טבריא call their own city רקת, both when mourning a Babylonian sage and when receiving a coffin brought for burial. If the locals call טבריא 'רקת', then רקת must be טבריא.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there anyone who says...? (expresses surprise at a view)
A code name for בבל (from ירמיה כה:כו)
They eulogize him
They bring up the coffin (to ארץ ישראל for burial)
The dead of the deep (people from low-lying בבל)

steps.confusionAlert: 'הכא' (here) means בבל, where רבא lives, and 'התם' (there) means טבריא in ארץ ישראל. Don't mix up which place is which.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: מִי אִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
phrases.english: Rava said: Is there anyone who says
that Rakkath is not Tiberias?
But when a great man dies here (in Babylonia),
there (in Tiberias) they eulogize him like this:
"Great was he in Sheshakh (Babylonia),
and he had a name in Rakkath."
And when they bring up a coffin to there,
they eulogize him like this:
Lovers of the remnants, residents of Rakkath,
go out and receive the dead of the deep (Babylonia).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִי אִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר רַקַּת לָאו טְבֶרְיָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the identification of רקת as ציפורי from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רקת is ציפורי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The residents of טבריא themselves call their city רקת in standard eulogies, so רקת must be טבריא.

steps.title: More proof: the eulogy for רבי זירא
steps.stepSummary: A story strengthens רבא's point. At רבי זירא's funeral, the eulogizer had רקת (the city where he lived and died) mourn its loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי זירא died, a certain eulogizer opened with: 'The land of שנער (בבל) conceived and gave birth to him; the land of the deer (ארץ ישראל) raised her delight. Woe to her, said רקת, for she has lost her precious treasure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more example showing that people called טבריא 'רקת'. רבי זירא was born in בבל and lived in טבריא, and the eulogy calls that city רקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא grew up in בבל, moved to ארץ ישראל, and was active in טבריא. When the eulogizer has 'רקת' lament losing him, he is speaking about טבריא. This adds a third piece of real-world usage behind רבא's objection.

keyTerms.meaning: His soul rested (he passed away)
A eulogizer
The land of Shinar, i.e., בבל
The land of the deer, i.e., ארץ ישראל
Her precious vessel/treasure

phrases.english: When Rabbi Zeira died,
a certain eulogizer opened for him:
The land of Shinar conceived and bore him,
the land of the deer raised her delight.
Woe unto her, said Rakkath,
for she has lost her precious instrument.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא, פְּתַח עֲלֵיהּ הַהוּא סַפְדָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another eulogy example to support רבא's objection.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The eulogy delivered for רבי זירא, in which רקת mourns him

steps.title: Revised identification: רקת is טבריא
steps.stepSummary: Since the first view fell, a new identification is given: חמת is the hot springs of גרר, רקת is טבריא, and כנרת is גינוסר. The name רקת is explained as praise of the city's residents.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה said: חמת is the hot springs of גרר, רקת is טבריא, and כנרת is גינוסר. Why is it called רקת? Because even the 'empty' people there are full of מצוות like a pomegranate is full of seeds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the first identification and replaces it with a new one that fits רבא's proofs. רקת is now טבריא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' signals that the earlier view is abandoned. Because רקת is now טבריא, חמת must be somewhere else, so it becomes the nearby hot springs of גרר. The new name explanation is a word-play: רקת sounds like 'ריקנין' (empty people), and even they are full of מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the previous view and offers a new one)
The hot springs of Gerar (near טבריא)
Empty ones, i.e., the least accomplished people
Full of מצוות like a pomegranate (is full of seeds)

steps.whatToRemember: The accepted identification is רקת = טבריא, חמת = the hot springs of גרר, and כנרת = גינוסר.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabba said:
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the name in round brackets, and some versions say רבא here.

phrases.english: Hammath is the hot springs of Gerar,
Rakkath is Tiberias,
Chinnereth is Ginosar.
And why was it called Rakkath?
Because even the empty ones in it
are full of מצוות like a pomegranate.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר (רַבָּה): חַמַּת זוֹ חַמֵּי גְרָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected identification of step 1 with one that fits the proofs in steps 2-3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חמת = חמי גרר, רקת = טבריא, כנרת = גינוסר. The name רקת praises even the simplest residents as full of מצוות.
steps.whyThisMatters: Knowing that טבריא is the biblical רקת, listed among the ערי מבצר in ספר יהושע, bears on the question of whether טבריא is a city walled since the days of יהושע for reading the מגילה.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: why the city is called טבריא
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says the city's real name is רקת. It is called טבריא because it sits at the center (טבור) of ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: רקת is its real name. Why is it called טבריא? Because it sits at the navel (center) of ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that רקת is accepted as טבריא, רבי ירמיה explains the second name. He says רקת is the original name and 'טבריא' is a nickname.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question flips direction. Before, the גמרא asked why טבריא is called רקת. Now רבי ירמיה treats רקת as the true name and explains 'טבריא' through a word-play on טבור (navel/center).

keyTerms.meaning: Rakkath is its (true) name
Its navel, i.e., its center point

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
Rakkath is its name,
and why was it called Tiberias?
Because it sits in the navel (center)
of Eretz Yisrael.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that רקת is טבריא by explaining the name טבריא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The true name is רקת. 'טבריא' comes from טבור, because the city is at the center of ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: רבא: טבריא means its appearance is good
steps.stepSummary: רבא also holds that the real name is רקת. He explains 'טבריא' as 'טובה ראייתה', meaning it is beautiful to look at.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רקת is its real name. Why is it called טבריא? Because its appearance is good.
steps.whatsHappening: A second explanation of the name טבריא is given, in disagreement with רבי ירמיה's word-play.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא agrees that רקת is the original name, but he reads 'טבריא' as a contraction of 'טובה ראייתה', 'its sight is good'. The disagreement is only about the source of the nickname, not about which city it is.

keyTerms.meaning: That its appearance is good (word-play on טבריא)

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone now agrees רקת is טבריא. רבי ירמיה and רבא only differ on why it is also called טבריא: 'center' (טבור) or 'good-looking' (טובה ראייתה).

phrases.english: Rava said:
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the name in round brackets, and some name a different speaker here.

phrases.english: Rakkath is its name,
and why was it called Tiberias?
Because its appearance is good.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative explanation to רבי ירמיה's for the name טבריא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The true name is רקת. 'טבריא' means 'טובה ראייתה', its appearance is good.

steps.title: זעירא identifies קטרון as ציפורי
steps.stepSummary: זעירא says the biblical city קטרון is the city of ציפורי. He explains that the name comes from its position high on a mountain, like a bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירא said: קטרון is ציפורי. Why is it called ציפורי? Because it sits on top of a mountain like a bird (צפור).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps matching place names from תנ״ך to known cities. זעירא now says that קטרון is ציפורי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new identification, like the earlier ones about רקת and טבריא. זעירא also explains the name ציפורי: the city sits high up like a bird perched on a mountain.

keyTerms.meaning: A city mentioned in ספר שופטים
A major city in the גליל
A bird

phrases.english: Zeira said: Kitron is Tzippori.
And why was it called Tzippori?
Because it sits on top of the mountain like a bird.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of biblical place identifications with a new city.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קטרון is ציפורי, named for sitting high on a mountain like a bird.

steps.title: Challenge: קטרון was in זבולון's territory, and זבולון complained about his land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions זעירא. קטרון was in זבולון's portion, and זבולון resented his portion because נפתלי got better fields.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is קטרון really ציפורי? But קטרון was in זבולון's portion, as it says: 'זבולון did not drive out the inhabitants of קטרון or the inhabitants of נהלול.' And זבולון was resentful about his portion, as it says: 'זבולון was a people that risked its life to death.' Why? Because 'נפתלי was on the high places of the field.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge against זעירא. It sets up two facts: קטרון belonged to זבולון, and זבולון was unhappy with his land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two verses show that קטרון was in זבולון's land and that זבולון complained his land was poor compared to נפתלי's fields. The hidden question is this: ציפורי was an excellent city, so if it were in זבולון's portion, why would he complain? The גמרא states that question openly in step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: In the tribal territory of זבולון
Did not drive out
Resentful of his portion
Risked his life; here read as expressing bitterness
High places of the field, meaning good farmland

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge is not finished here. The story about זבולון in steps 9-12 explains his complaint. The actual punchline, that ציפורי was too good a city for him to complain about, comes in step 13.

phrases.english: And is Kitron Tzippori?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא קִטְרוֹן בְּחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל זְבוּלוּן הֲוַאי,
phrases.english: But Kitron was in the territory of Zebulun,
as it is written: 'Zebulun did not drive out'

phrases.aramaic: אֶת יוֹשְׁבֵי קִטְרוֹן וְאֶת יוֹשְׁבֵי נַהֲלוֹל״,
phrases.english: 'the inhabitants of Kitron or the inhabitants of Nahalol,'
and Zebulun was resentful of his portion,
as it says: 'Zebulun was a people that risked its life to death,'
What is the reason?
Because 'Naphtali was on the high places of the field.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקִטְרוֹן, צִיפּוֹרִי הִיא? וְהָא קִטְרוֹן בְּחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל זְבוּלוּן הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges זעירא's identification in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: זעירא's claim that קטרון is ציפורי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קטרון was in זבולון's land, and זבולון complained that his land was poor. ציפורי was an excellent place, so it does not fit a portion he complained about. The attack is stated explicitly in step 13.

steps.title: זבולון complains to הקדוש ברוך הוא and is answered
steps.stepSummary: זבולון complains that his brothers got fields, vineyards and good land, while he got mountains, hills, seas and rivers. הקדוש ברוך הוא answers that everyone will need him because of the חלזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: זבולון said before הקדוש ברוך הוא: Master of the world! To my brothers You gave fields and vineyards, and to me mountains and hills. To my brothers You gave lands, and to me seas and rivers! He answered: Everyone will need you because of the חלזון, as it says: '[They shall call peoples to the mountain]… and the treasures hidden in the sand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that explains the verse about זבולון's resentment. It shows exactly what he complained about and how הקדוש ברוך הוא comforted him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זבולון felt cheated because his land was rough and watery instead of farmland. The answer is that his seas hold something everyone needs: the חלזון, the source of the blue dye for ציצית. A verse from ברכת משה supports this.

keyTerms.meaning: Master of the world
Fields and vineyards
Seas and rivers
Sea creature that is the source of תכלת dye
Treasures hidden in the sand (דברים לג:יט)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר זְבוּלוּן לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Zebulun said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the Universe,
to my brothers You gave fields and vineyards,
and to me You gave mountains and hills!
To my brothers You gave lands,
and to me You gave seas and rivers!

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: כּוּלָּן צְרִיכִין לָךְ עַל יְדֵי חִלָּזוֹן,
phrases.english: He said to him: All will need you because of the ḥilazon,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״[עַמִּים הַר יִקְרָאוּ] וּשְׂפוּנֵי טְמוּנֵי חוֹל״.
phrases.english: as it says: '[They shall call peoples to the mountain]… and the hidden treasures of the sand.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר זְבוּלוּן לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the content of זבולון's resentment mentioned in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זבולון's land was hilly and watery, but it held the חלזון, which everyone needs.

steps.title: רב יוסף explains each word of the verse
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches what each word stands for. שפוני is the חלזון, טמוני is the טרית fish, and חול is white glass made from sand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף taught: 'שפוני' is the חלזון, 'טמוני' is the טרית fish, and 'חול' is white glass.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף breaks the verse into three words and matches each to a treasure in זבולון's waters and shores.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse becomes a list of three valuable resources in זבולון's territory: the dye-producing חלזון, a type of fish, and sand for making white glass. This shows how rich his 'poor' land really was.

keyTerms.meaning: A small fish, like a sardine or tuna
White, clear glass

phrases.english: Rav Yosef taught:
'Treasures' — this is the ḥilazon,
'Hidden' — this is the tarit fish,
'Sand' — this is white glass.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the verse quoted at the end of step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שפוני means the חלזון, טמוני means the טרית, and חול means white glass.

steps.title: זבולון asks how he will know if others take his goods
steps.stepSummary: זבולון asks הקדוש ברוך הוא who will tell him if people take these treasures without paying.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said before Him: Master of the world, who will let me know?
steps.whatsHappening: זבולון raises a worry: his treasures are hidden in the sea and sand, so people could take them secretly. This question sets up הקדוש ברוך הוא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having valuable resources is only useful if others cannot steal them unnoticed. זבולון wants some way to know who took from him without paying.

keyTerms.meaning: Who will inform me?

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the Universe,
who will inform me?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם מִי מוֹדִיעֵנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: זבולון continues the conversation, worried about theft of the treasures listed in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How זבולון will know whether someone took his resources without paying.

steps.title: The sign: whoever takes without paying will not prosper
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא answers with the verse 'There they will offer righteous offerings.' The sign is that anyone who takes from זבולון without paying will have no success in his business.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'There they shall offer offerings of righteousness.' This will be a sign for you: anyone who takes from you without paying will not succeed at all in his business.
steps.whatsHappening: הקדוש ברוך הוא answers זבולון's worry. He promises a sign: thieves of זבולון's goods will fail in business.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word צדק (righteousness/honesty) in the verse hints that only people who deal honestly and pay will prosper from these goods. זבולון does not need to catch thieves himself, because their businesses will fail. This finishes the story, and the גמרא then returns to its challenge about קטרון.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of righteousness; hints at honest payment
A sign
Without payment
Business, trade

steps.whatToRemember: זבולון complained that his land was mountains and seas. הקדוש ברוך הוא told him it holds the חלזון, the טרית and glass-sand, and that anyone who takes them without paying will fail. This background explains why the גמרא doubts that the fine city ציפורי could be קטרון in זבולון's portion.

phrases.english: He said to him: 'There they shall sacrifice offerings of righteousness,'
this shall be a sign for you:
anyone who takes from you without payment
will not prosper in his business at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers זבולון's question from step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse is a sign: whoever takes זבולון's resources without paying will not succeed in business.

steps.title: If קטרון is ציפורי, why would זבולון complain?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sharpens its challenge: ציפורי was excellent land, so if it was in זבולון's portion, he had nothing to complain about.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think קטרון is ציפורי, why was זבולון upset about his portion? ציפורי was very, very good land!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues attacking זעירא's claim that קטרון is ציפורי. If ציפורי was in זבולון's land, his complaint makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 9, זבולון complained that he got only mountains and seas. But ציפורי was known as top-quality land. So either ציפורי was not in his portion, or his complaint is hard to understand.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you think (if it enters your mind)
Tzippori, an important city in the Galil
Complains, is resentful
Very much better, far superior

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that Kitron is Tzippori,
why was he resentful of his portion?
But Tzippori was
something vastly superior!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ קִטְרוֹן זוֹ צִיפּוֹרִי, אַמַּאי מִתְרַעֵם עַל מִדּוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the challenge from Step 8 after the side discussion about זבולון's treasures in Steps 9-12.
steps.kashyaTarget: זעירא's identification of קטרון as ציפורי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ציפורי was excellent land. If it belonged to זבולון, his complaint about getting poor land makes no sense.

steps.title: ציפורי did flow with milk and honey
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible defense. Someone might say ציפורי was not truly fertile, but ריש לקיש saw a huge fertile area there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say ציפורי did not have land flowing with milk and honey, ריש לקיש said: I saw the milk-and-honey land of ציפורי myself, and it was sixteen מיל by sixteen מיל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא imagines a possible answer to its question and knocks it down right away. ציפורי really was very fertile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The possible answer is that ציפורי was not good land after all. ריש לקיש's eyewitness report proves it was fertile over a large area, 16 by 16 מיל. So the challenge from Step 13 stays strong.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a possible answer)
Flowing with milk and honey, very fertile land
I myself saw it
A mil, a unit of distance

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's real answer. 'וכי תימא' raises a possible answer only to reject it, which makes the question stronger.

phrases.english: And if you would say that it did not have
land flowing with milk and honey,
but didn't Reish Lakish say:
I myself saw
the land flowing with milk and honey of Tzippori,
and it was sixteen mil
by sixteen mil!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּלֵית בַּהּ זָבַת חָלָב וּדְבָשׁ, וְהָאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a possible defense against the challenge in Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The possible claim that ציפורי was not fertile land
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: ריש לקיש saw that ציפורי had a large fertile area, 16 by 16 מיל.

steps.title: ציפורי's fertile land was more than a fair share
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a second defense. Maybe זבולון's fertile land was smaller than his brothers' share? No. רבי יוחנן's measurement of all of ארץ ישראל shows ציפורי's area was more than one tribe's fair share.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say his fertile land was not as big as his brothers' land, רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: I saw the milk-and-honey land of all ארץ ישראל. It stretched from בי כובי to the fortress of תולבקני, 22 פרסאות long and 6 פרסאות wide!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second possible defense and rejects it with numbers. ציפורי alone had more than an average tribe's share of fertile land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פרסה is 4 מיל, so ציפורי was 4 by 4 פרסאות, which is 16 square פרסאות. All of ארץ ישראל's fertile land was 22 by 6, which is 132 square פרסאות. Split among 12 tribes, that is 11 each, so זבולון actually got more than his fair share.

keyTerms.meaning: Large, plentiful
Like his brothers' (shares)
Parsaot, units of distance (each is 4 mil)
Length
Width

phrases.english: And if you would say that it was not as large,
his share, as his brothers' shares,
but didn't Rabba bar bar Chana say
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
I myself saw

phrases.aramaic: זָבַת חָלָב וּדְבָשׁ דְּכׇל אַרְעָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: the land flowing with milk and honey of all the Land of Israel,
and it was like the distance from Bei Kovei
to the fortress of Tulbakni,
twenty-two parasangs in length,
and six parasangs in width!
phrases.notes: 22 × 6 = 132 square פרסאות. Divided by 12 tribes, that is 11 each. ציפורי had 16.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּלָא נְפִישָׁא דִּידֵיהּ כְּדַאֲחוּהּ, וְהָאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a second possible defense, after Step 14 blocked the first.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The possible claim that זבולון's fertile area was smaller than the other tribes' areas
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The math from רבי יוחנן's measurement shows ציפורי's 16 square פרסאות was more than the average 11 per tribe.

steps.title: זבולון still preferred fields and vineyards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: even with ציפורי's rich land, זבולון wanted ordinary fields and vineyards, like his brothers had.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, fields and vineyards were better in his eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא gives its real answer. זבולון's complaint was about the kind of land he got, not the amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זבולון did have rich land at ציפורי, but it was in hilly country and hard to farm. He wanted flat fields and vineyards like נפתלי had. So זעירא's claim that קטרון is ציפורי can stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Even so
Fields and vineyards

phrases.english: Even so,
fields and vineyards were preferable to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי, שָׂדוֹת וּכְרָמִים עֲדִיפָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge built in Steps 13-15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the complaint as being about the type of land, not its quality or size
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought זבולון complained that his land was poor, which does not fit with owning ציפורי.
steps.terutzMaskana: זבולון had rich land but wanted flat fields and vineyards, so he could own ציפורי and still complain.

steps.title: The verse about נפתלי's fields supports the answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the verse fits this answer: נפתלי is described as being 'on the high places of the field.' So זבולון's complaint was about fields.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse is precise this way too, as it is written: 'And נפתלי was on the high places of the field.' Learn from this that it is so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support from the verse for its answer and closes the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse stresses that נפתלי had 'field,' meaning farmland. This matches the idea that זבולון was jealous of fields specifically. 'שמע מינה' confirms the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also precise (the wording supports this)
The high places of the field
Learn from it, conclude from it

steps.whatToRemember: זעירא's claim that קטרון is ציפורי survives. זבולון had rich land, but his complaint was that he lacked flat fields and vineyards like נפתלי had.

phrases.english: It is also precise, as it is written:
"And Naphtali was on the high places of the field."
phrases.notes: שופטים ה:יח, the same verse that speaks about זבולון.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in Step 16 from the wording of the verse.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that זבולון's complaint was about fields and vineyards

steps.title: עקרון is קסרי, the thorn in ישראל's side
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו teaches that the verse 'עקרון shall be uprooted' refers to קסרי, a city that troubled the Jews and was later conquered by the חשמונאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: 'And עקרון shall be uprooted' means קסרי, daughter of אדום, which sits among the sands. It was a spike stuck in Israel's side in the days of the Greeks. When the חשמונאי kingdom grew strong and beat them, people called it 'the captured tower of Shir.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. The גמרא keeps identifying places named in the תנ״ך, and רבי אבהו explains a verse about עקרון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו reads the prophecy against עקרון as being about קסרי, the center of Roman (אדום) rule. He gives its history: it troubled the Jews under the Greeks and was captured by the חשמונאים. The prophecy says it will one day be uprooted.

keyTerms.meaning: And Ekron shall be uprooted (Zephaniah 2:4)
Caesarea, daughter of Edom (Rome)
A spike stuck in, a constant troublemaker
The Hasmonean kingdom
The captured tower of Shir

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
"And Ekron shall be uprooted" —
this is Caesarea, daughter of Edom,
which is situated among the sands,

phrases.aramaic: וְהִיא הָיְתָה יָתֵד תְּקוּעָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בִּימֵי יְווֹנִים.
phrases.english: and it was a spike stuck into Israel in the days of the Greeks.
And when the Hasmonean kingdom grew strong and defeated them,
they would call it "the captured tower of Shir."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new identification of a place in the Tanach, continuing the general theme of matching verses to places.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The prophecy about עקרון refers to קסרי, the Roman city that troubled Israel and was conquered by the חשמונאים.

steps.title: The idol worship of the nations will be removed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא explains a פסוק in זכריה. 'His blood from his mouth' refers to their houses of altars, and 'his detestable things from between his teeth' refers to their houses of stone piles used for idol worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: What does this verse mean: 'I will take away his blood from his mouth, and his detestable things from between his teeth, and he too will remain for our God'? 'I will take away his blood from his mouth' means their house of altars. 'His detestable things from between his teeth' means their house of stone piles.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רבי יוסי בר חנינא explains a פסוק in זכריה piece by piece, starting with the two phrases about removing idol worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks in picture language about 'blood' and 'detestable things' in the mouth. רבי יוסי בר חנינא says these are real places: the altars where they offered sacrifices to idols, and the stone piles they built for idol worship. In the future, ה׳ will remove both.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written? This is the standard opening for explaining a פסוק.
And I will remove / take away
His detestable things, meaning idols or idol worship
House of altars, a place for sacrifices to idols
House of piles, a place where stones were heaped up for idol worship

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"And I will take away his blood from his mouth,
and his detestable things from between his teeth,
and he too will remain for our God."
"And I will take away his blood from his mouth":
this is their house of altars.
"And his detestable things from between his teeth":
this is their house of stone piles.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of prophecies about the cities of the nations (עקרון in step 18), now using a פסוק in זכריה that also mentions עקרון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'blood' and 'detestable things' in the פסוק are the idolatrous altars and stone piles of the nations, which ה׳ will remove.

steps.title: The gathering places of אדום will become places of Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא continues. 'He too will remain for our God' refers to the בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות in אדום. 'He will be like a chief in Judah, and עקרון like a יבוסי' refers to the theaters and circuses of אדום, where the leaders of יהודה will one day teach תורה in public.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He too will remain for our God' refers to the בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות in אדום. 'He will be like a chief in יהודה, and עקרון like a יבוסי' refers to the theaters and circuses in אדום, where the leaders of יהודה will one day teach תורה to the public.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר חנינא finishes explaining the same פסוק. This part describes what will remain after the idol worship is removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק spoke about removal. This half speaks about what remains and is transformed. The בתי כנסיות in אדום will stay holy, and even the theaters and circuses, places of non-Jewish entertainment, will become places where תורה is taught publicly.

keyTerms.meaning: Synagogues
Study halls
Edom, which the Sages use to mean Rome
Theaters and circuses, the Roman places of entertainment
The leaders / officers of Judah

steps.confusionAlert: This is still the same teaching of רבי יוסי בר חנינא from step 19. It is not a new speaker. He is explaining the rest of the same פסוק.

phrases.english: "And he too will remain for our God":

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ בָּתֵּי כְנֵסִיּוֹת וּבָתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת שֶׁבֶּאֱדוֹם.
phrases.english: these are the synagogues and study halls that are in Edom.
"And he will be like a chief in Judah, and Ekron like a Jebusite":
these are the theaters and circuses that are in Edom,
where the leaders of Judah are destined
to teach Torah in them to the public.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יוסי בר חנינא's explanation of the same פסוק, moving from what will be removed to what will remain and be transformed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The synagogues of אדום will remain holy, and its theaters and circuses will one day become places of public Torah teaching.

steps.title: לשם is פמייס, and עקרון is קסרי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק identifies two places. לשם is the city later called פמייס. 'עקרון shall be uprooted' refers to קסרי, the daughter of אדום, which was a capital city of kings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: לשם is פמייס. 'עקרון shall be uprooted' refers to קסרי, the daughter of אדום, which was a capital city of kings.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teacher, רבי יצחק, matches names of places in תנ״ך with the cities known in his own time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לשם, the city that שבט דן conquered, is identified as פמייס. Like רבי אבהו in step 18, רבי יצחק says 'עקרון shall be uprooted' means קסרי, and he adds that it was a royal capital of אדום.

keyTerms.meaning: Leshem, a city conquered by שבט דן (יהושע יט:מז)
Pamyas, the Talmudic-era name of לשם
Caesarea, 'daughter of Edom', a center of Roman rule
Metropolis, a capital city

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Leshem, this is Pamyas.
"Ekron shall be uprooted":
this is Caesarea, the daughter of Edom,
which was a capital city of kings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new speaker identifying more places. It repeats and expands רבי אבהו's identification of עקרון with קסרי from step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לשם is פמייס, and the עקרון that will be uprooted is קסרי, the royal capital of אדום.

steps.title: Two explanations of 'capital city of kings'
steps.stepSummary: Two opinions explain what 'capital city of kings' means. One says kings were raised in קסרי. The other says kings were appointed from among its people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it means that kings were raised there. Others say it means that kings were appointed from there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the phrase 'capital city of kings' from step 21 and brings two ways to understand it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view says the sons of kings grew up and were trained in קסרי. The second view says the rulers of אדום were chosen from the citizens of קסרי. Either way, the city was the center of royal power.

keyTerms.meaning: That kings were raised in it
That kings were appointed from it

phrases.english: There are those who say:
that kings were raised in it;
and there are those who say:
that kings were appointed from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the phrase 'מטרופולין של מלכים' from רבי יצחק's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Capital of kings' means either that kings were raised in קסרי or that kings were appointed from its people.

steps.title: קסרי and ירושלים cannot both thrive or both fall
steps.stepSummary: If someone tells you that both קסרי and ירושלים are destroyed, or that both are flourishing, do not believe him. If he says one is destroyed and the other is settled, believe him.
steps.simpleTranslation: קסרי and ירושלים: if a person tells you that both are destroyed, do not believe him. If he says both are settled, do not believe him. If he says קסרי is destroyed and ירושלים is settled, or ירושלים is destroyed and קסרי is settled, believe him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא teaches a rule about the opposite fortunes of קסרי, which stands for Rome, and ירושלים. The next step brings the פסוק that proves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cities are on a seesaw. When one goes up, the other goes down. So any report that both are in the same state must be false, and only a report that they are in opposite states can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: Both were destroyed
Both are settled / flourishing
Do not believe

steps.whyThisMatters: This expresses a major idea in אגדה: the rise of רומי is tied to the fall of ירושלים, and the rebuilding of ירושלים is tied to רומי's fall.

phrases.english: Caesarea and Jerusalem:
if a person says to you:
"Both are destroyed", do not believe him.
"Both are settled", do not believe him.
"Caesarea is destroyed and Jerusalem is settled,"
or "Jerusalem is destroyed and Caesarea is settled", believe him,

steps.triggerLanguage: קֵסָרִי וִירוּשָׁלַיִם, אִם יֹאמַר לְךָ אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the identification of קסרי as the royal center of אדום, and contrasts it with ירושלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קסרי and ירושלים always have opposite fortunes. One thrives only when the other is in ruins.

steps.title: The verse 'I shall be filled from the ruined one'
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק 'אמלאה החרבה', 'I shall be filled from the one laid waste'. When one city is full, the other is ruined, and the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'I shall be filled, she is laid waste.' If this one is full, that one is ruined. If that one is full, this one is ruined.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק from יחזקאל to prove the rule from step 23 that the two cities cannot thrive together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, צור, which represents Rome, says about ירושלים: 'I will be filled from her ruin.' This shows that the enemy's fullness comes from ירושלים's destruction, so the two can never both be full or both be empty.

keyTerms.meaning: I shall be filled; she is laid waste (יחזקאל כו:ב)
Full / filled, meaning thriving
Destroyed / laid waste

steps.whatToRemember: The prophets describe the future removal of idol worship and even the transformation of Roman places into places of תורה. קסרי, the royal city of Rome, and ירושלים are always opposites: when one is built up, the other is in ruins.

phrases.english: as it is said: "I shall be filled; she is laid waste."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל כו:ב, spoken by צור about ירושלים

phrases.english: If this one is full, that one is laid waste;
if that one is full, this one is laid waste.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the scriptural source for the rule about קסרי and ירושלים in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that קסרי and ירושלים cannot thrive or fall together.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל כו:ב, 'אמלאה החרבה'. The enemy is filled from ירושלים's ruin.

steps.title: A second verse: one nation grows strong from the other
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק offers a different פסוק to prove that ירושלים and קסרי cannot both flourish at once: 'ולאום מלאום יאמץ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: we learn it from here: 'And one nation shall be stronger than the other nation.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second source for the rule in Step 23, that when one of the two cities is up, the other is down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 learned the rule from 'אמלאה החרבה'. רב נחמן בר יצחק uses a פסוק about יעקב and עשו while they were still in רבקה's womb. It says one nation will be strong 'from' the other, meaning one gains strength only as the other loses it. The rule stays the same. Only the source changes.

keyTerms.meaning: From here. A formula for bringing a different source for the same idea.
A nation. Here it means the nations that come from יעקב and עשו.
Will become strong.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: from here
"And one nation shall be stronger than the other nation."
phrases.notes: בראשית כה:כג, said to רבקה about יעקב and עשו.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different פסוק for the same rule that Step 24 proved from 'אמלאה החרבה'.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that ירושלים and קסרי cannot both be destroyed or both flourish at the same time.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית כה:כג, 'ולאום מלאום יאמץ': one nation's strength comes at the cost of the other.
steps.whatToRemember: Two פסוקים, one idea. When ישראל is up, אדום is down, and when אדום is up, ישראל is down.

steps.title: יצחק pleads for mercy on עשו
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק reads ישעיהו 26:10 as a conversation between יצחק אבינו and הקדוש ברוך הוא. יצחק asks that עשו be shown favor. Each part of the פסוק is God's answer or יצחק's reply, until יצחק agrees that עשו will not see God's majesty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: What does the פסוק mean, 'Let the wicked be shown favor; he has not learned righteousness'? יצחק said before God: Master of the world, let עשו be shown favor. God answered: He is wicked! יצחק said: 'Has he not learned righteousness?' Is there no merit to be found in him? God said: 'In the land of uprightness he will do wrong,' meaning he will destroy ארץ ישראל. יצחק said: If so, 'let him not see the majesty of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching of רבי יצחק about עשו. He turns one פסוק into a back-and-forth conversation between יצחק and God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic of אדום leads into this related אגדה. Each phrase of the פסוק belongs to a different speaker. יצחק asks for favor and points to some merit in עשו. God answers that עשו will destroy ארץ ישראל. Once יצחק hears this, he himself agrees that עשו should not see God's glory.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written? This opens an explanation of a פסוק.
Let him be shown favor or grace.
Master of the world. A way of addressing God in prayer.
The land of uprightness, meaning ארץ ישראל.
He will act wrongly or destructively.
The majesty and glory of God.

steps.confusionAlert: In the simple reading of the פסוק, 'בל למד צדק' is a statement: 'he has not learned righteousness.' In this dialogue, יצחק says those words as a question: 'Has he truly learned no righteousness at all?' He is pleading that there must be some merit in עשו. He is not agreeing that עשו is wicked.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said: What is the meaning of what is written:
"Let the wicked be shown favor; he has not learned righteousness."

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר יִצְחָק לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Isaac said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
phrases.notes: This is יצחק אבינו, the father of עשו.

phrases.english: Master of the world, let Esau be shown favor.
He [God] said to him: He is wicked!
He [Isaac] said to Him: "Has he not learned righteousness?"
phrases.notes: Meaning: is there no merit at all to be found in him?

phrases.english: He [God] said to him: "In the land of uprightness he will do wrong."

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אִם כֵּן, ״בַּל יִרְאֶה גֵּאוּת ה׳״.
phrases.english: He [Isaac] said to Him: If so, "let him not see the majesty of the Lord."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rise and fall of אדום to a new אגדה of רבי יצחק about עשו himself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ישעיהו 26:10 is a dialogue. יצחק pleads for עשו, God shows that עשו will destroy ארץ ישראל, and יצחק then agrees that עשו will not see God's majesty.

steps.title: יעקב asks God not to fulfill עשו's evil desires
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains תהלים 140:9 as יעקב's prayer that עשו not receive what his heart desires. He then begins to explain 'זממו אל תפק', and the sentence continues into the next passage.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: What does the פסוק mean, 'Do not grant, ה׳, the desires of the wicked; do not let his plan succeed, so they will not rise up, סלה'? יעקב said before God: Master of the world, do not give the wicked עשו what his heart wants. 'Do not let his זמם loose': this is...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives a second explanation of a פסוק, this time as a prayer of יעקב about עשו. This passage ends in the middle of a sentence, and the next passage tells us what 'זממו' refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the earlier teaching. There, יצחק pleaded for עשו. Here, יעקב prays against עשו's plans. The first half of the פסוק asks that עשו not get his heart's desire, meaning his wish to destroy ישראל. The word 'זממו' will be read as a 'muzzle' that keeps עשו in check, and the גמרא is about to name who or what that is.

keyTerms.meaning: The desires or cravings of.
His scheme. It is also read as 'his muzzle' (זמם), which holds him back.
Do not let it succeed, or do not let it loose.
The desire of his heart.

steps.confusionAlert: This passage stops at the word 'זוֹ' ('this is...'). The explanation of what 'זממו' refers to comes on the next amud. Do not think the teaching ends here.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said: What is the meaning of what is written:
"Do not grant, O Lord, the desires of the wicked;
do not further his scheme, so they will not rise up. Selah."

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר יַעֲקֹב לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Jacob said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world, do not give
to the wicked Esau the desire of his heart.
"Do not let loose his muzzle": this is...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second explanation by רבי יצחק of a פסוק about עשו. It moves from יצחק's plea for him to יעקב's prayer against him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תהלים 140:9 is יעקב's prayer that עשו not receive his heart's desire and that the 'muzzle' restraining him not be removed. What that muzzle is comes on the next amud.
